newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lai Sun raises HK$1.98 bln in shr issue.
newsitem.headline: Lai Sun raises HK$1.98 bln in shr issue.

text.p: Lai Sun Development Co Ltd said on Thursday it would issue 165 million new shares to its parent Lai Sun Garment (International) Ltd at HK$12.00 per share after Lai Sun Garment places the same number of shares.
The company said in a statement it would issue a further 79.05 million new shares to its chairman Lim Por Yen to buy the remaining 50 percent of Causeway Bay Plaza 1, which it does not already own.
Lai Sun Garment would place 165 million existing Lai Sun Development shares to professional and institutional investors at HK$12.00 per share before subscribing to the new shares.
Lai Sun Development said it will use the proceeds of the new share issue of about HK$1.98 billion before expenses to replenish its Hong Kong land bank and for working capital.

It said it would also buy the remaining 50 percent stake in its 50-percent owned associate Lucky Strike Investment Ltd from Lim for HK$1 billion, which would be paid through the issue of 79.05 million new shares at HK$12.65 per share.
Trading in shares of Lai Sun Development and Lai Sun Garment was suspended on Wednesday. The shares closed at HK$12.65 and HK$11.75 respectively on Tuesday and are due to resume trading on Thursday.
Lucky Strike's only major asset is a 27 storey office and commercial building -- Causeway Bay Plaza 1 -- covering a total gross floor area of 248,000 square feet, in Causeway Bay on Hong Kong island.
The property was valued by an independent valuer at an open market value of HK$2.55 billion as of January 14, 1997, Lai Sun Development said.

On completion of the deal, Lim and his family's direct shareholding in Lai Sun Development will increase to 12.23 percent from a current 6.28 percent, while Lai Sun Garment's holding in Lai Sun Development will be diluted to 38.86 percent from 50.32 percent.
The shareholding of Lim and his family in Lai Sun Garment would remain unchanged at 46.89 percent.
